_about: Regime-aligned cash sleeve compositions. The allocation engine reads this to suggest where to hold the cash floor — TIPS, gold, money-market ETFs, short-duration treasuries — instead of letting cash sit idle. Each composition lists ETF tickers with target weights, an est_yield, and a one-line rationale. Yields are illustrative as of April 2026; verify on broker before acting.

Goldilocks.label: Goldilocks · Q1 — Growth ↑ Inflation ↓
Goldilocks.rationale: Risk-on regime — equities are the dominant return driver. Hold the cash floor in productive, liquid yield instruments so you don't drag returns sitting in zero-yield cash.

composition.why: Daily-liquid T-bill ETF. Yield resets with Fed Funds — a productive parking place that behaves like cash.
AAA-rated collateralised loan obligations. Higher yield than T-bills, floating rate, very low default history at AAA.
Treasury floaters reset every 3 months — rate-resilient if Fed holds higher for longer.

Reflation.label: Reflation · Q2 — Growth ↑ Inflation ↑
Reflation.rationale: Both growth and inflation rising. Real assets and commodities lead. The cash floor needs to earn the inflation premium rather than lose to it — TIPS adjust principal with CPI, gold benefits from negative real rates, commodity ETFs respond directly to price surprises.

composition.why: Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities — principal adjusts with CPI. The cleanest inflation hedge in ETF form.
Gold is the anchor hedge against negative real rates and currency debasement. No yield, but historical correlation to inflation surprises is strong.
Diversified commodity basket (energy, metals, agriculture). Highest correlation to inflation surprises of any liquid ETF.
Keep a daily-liquid base in Fed-Funds-tracking T-bills so you're not all in inflation-sensitive instruments.

Deflation.label: Deflation · Q3 — Growth ↓ Inflation ↓
Deflation.rationale: Growth and inflation both rolling over. Long-duration sovereign bonds shine — falling rates lift bond prices. Stretch duration in the cash sleeve to capture price appreciation, keep some short-duration for optionality.

composition.why: 20+ year Treasuries are the deflation hedge — they appreciate sharply when rates fall. Higher volatility than cash, but the ballast Vol III's All-Weather framework calls for.
Intermediate Treasuries — duration exposure without going all the way out the curve. Smaller drawdown risk than TLT.

composition.n: iShares Core US Aggregate Bond ETF
composition.why: Total bond market — Treasuries, agency mortgages, investment-grade corporates. Diversified credit + duration.
Keep daily liquidity for opportunistic deployment if equities reset.

Stagflation.label: Stagflation · Q4 — Growth ↓ Inflation ↑
Stagflation.rationale: The hardest regime. Equity multiples compress while bonds underperform inflation. Hard assets and short-duration cash are the historical winners. Avoid long duration, lean into gold and commodities, keep the rest in TIPS and floating-rate.

composition.why: Gold has historically been the single best stagflation asset. No yield, but the only liquid instrument that's both inflation-hedge and growth-resilient.
Inflation-protected real yield. Holds value even when growth disappoints.
Direct commodity exposure for the inflation side of the regime. Energy weighting helps if oil supply tightens.
Floaters reset with Fed Funds — if the Fed has to keep rates high to fight inflation, you keep the yield without taking duration risk.
Daily-liquid T-bills round out the sleeve and provide dry powder.

Unclassified.label: Unclassified · transitioning regime
Unclassified.rationale: When the regime is in transition or signals are mixed, keep the cash sleeve broadly diversified — productive yield with a small inflation hedge. Re-evaluate when growth or inflation breaks decisively.

composition.why: Default productive cash — daily liquid, Fed-Funds-tracking yield.
Modest inflation-hedge anchor in case the regime turns reflationary.
Rate-resilient base. Holds yield if Fed keeps rates higher for longer.
Pickup yield over T-bills with AAA credit and floating rate.
